chosen_actions.description: Continue and advance the in-progress transportation decision-support curriculum, now updated for the $0.12/mile RoboRide reality with 8-minute wait times. The curriculum segment this month addresses a more specific decision point than previous months: not 'should I sell my car' but 'I am in a retraining program with variable hours and I need to get to the program site and to any interim work — what is my actual transportation cost calculus.' This is the question that will determine whether people complete retraining or drop out mid-program. I am building a one-page decision tool that maps transit combinations against a person's specific schedule pattern — not a generic roboride endorsement, a real cost-benefit map. This goes into the Financial Triage Navigator session toolkit as a standard handout.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Design and preparation time. The one-page tool becomes a permanent resource in the navigator toolkit — compounding return on a fixed time investment.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The retraining pipeline is only as good as the people who complete it. Four people referred to retraining from my Financial Triage Navigator sessions. Transportation is the hidden cost that causes people to drop out before completion. If I can give navigators a tool that addresses this specific decision point — not in the abstract, but for the person sitting across from them — I reduce dropout risk for the people already in the pipeline. The $0.12 RoboRide price and 8-minute wait time is a genuinely improved option that people do not know how to evaluate yet. I help them evaluate it.
